+- **Which cell holds the single value the whole answer keys off.** When the instruction says "using
+  the year value shown", "for the selected name", "from the dropdown", there is usually more than one
+  cell that could plausibly be meant — a label's neighbour, a column of candidates, a header. Picking
+  the wrong one is invisible afterwards: every cell you write is then consistently wrong by the same
+  rule, and no check that compares your own numbers will notice. So print EVERY candidate with its

+  you are filling a column by extending a pattern — numbering rows, lettering sub-items, carrying a

 The task is not finished while any line of the check is still wrong.
 
-Never re-send a code block identical to one you already ran. If you are about to repeat yourself you
-have stopped making progress, and the information you need is in cells you have not printed yet.
+# 7. Every block must print something, or the turn is wasted
+
+The sandbox sends you back only what your code printed. So a block that computes and saves but prints
+nothing comes back as:
+
+```
+[Code executed successfully with no output]
+```
+
+That line tells you the code did not crash and NOTHING else — not what was written, not whether the
+lookup matched, not whether the file changed. It is the single most expensive thing that can happen in
+a turn, because the usual response to it is to send a slightly different version of the same block and
+get it again. Rollouts that hit it repeatedly are the ones that run out of turns having written a
+handful of cells.
+
+So, mechanically:
+
+- **End every block with a `print()` you can act on.** After a save, print the count of cells you
+  wrote and two or three of the actual values, read back from the saved file:
+  ```python
+  wb.save(OUT)
+  chk = openpyxl.load_workbook(OUT)[SHEET]
+  print("wrote", len(written), "cells |", [(a1, chk[a1].value) for a1 in written[:3]])
+  ```
+- **If a block comes back with no output, that is a bug in the block, not a result.** Do not re-send
+  it with a small change. Send a block that does nothing but PRINT the state you failed to look at:
+  the source cells with `repr()` and type, the lookup keys and how many matched, the length of the
+  list you built, and the first few target cells read back from the saved file. Then decide.
+- **Print your assumptions as you use them, not the conclusions.** `print("year", repr(year), "from
+  B3")` is worth more than `print("done")`, because the wrong cell for `year` is invisible in the
+  answer and obvious in the print.
+- **Never re-send a code block identical to one you already ran**, and treat a block that differs
+  only in a constant as identical. If you are about to repeat yourself you have stopped making
+  progress, and the information you need is in cells you have not printed yet.
+- **You have a limited number of turns.** If you are past the halfway point and the target cells are
+  still empty or unverified, stop refining and spend the next block writing the straightforward
+  version of the answer for EVERY cell your rule covers, then print it back. A complete answer you
+  can still see is worth more than a partial one you cannot.
+- **Printing the same correct answer twice is how a finished task fails.** The print exists so you can
+  READ it and then stop. If a block's output matches what the block before it printed, you are done —
+  the next reply must be no code block at all. Re-saving a file that is already right cannot improve
+  your score, and each repeat burns a turn you cannot get back. Compare this block's output to the
+  last one before writing anything: same output means finish, not refine.
